subject.title: [Feature]: Add a standard AISP/AISOP proposal contract for Skill Workshop

question: Should Skill Workshop get a core-owned machine-readable proposal lifecycle contract, and if so should it be OpenClaw-native, AISP/AISOP, or externalized as a ClawHub/bundle reference artifact?
rationale: The source gap is real, but choosing the contract authority affects core scope and security governance rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: OpenClaw-native docs/test contract
options.body: Add a compact contract document or fixture plus tests that mirror the existing Skill Workshop service invariants, with no runtime AISP dependency.

options.title: External AISP/ClawHub artifact
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core as-is and publish the AISP/AISOP reference package externally as a bundle-style artifact until maintainers want core validation hooks.

options.title: Decline broad contract for now
options.body: Keep the existing docs and service tests as the source of truth and handle only narrower lifecycle validation requests such as runtime testing separately.

recommendation.title: OpenClaw-native docs/test contract
recommendation.body: Add a compact contract document or fixture plus tests that mirror the existing Skill Workshop service invariants, with no runtime AISP dependency.

likelyOwner.reason: The Shakker-authored commits introduced the central Skill Workshop proposal store, CLI, and Gateway surfaces that would be formalized by this decision.
